# SQL fixtures

Projects read by `test/unit/sql.test.js`. `expected/<fixture>.json` is the exact output of `parsers/sql.js` with `{ details: true, columnSources: true, git: false }`, one line per column, relation and index: it was written by the parser, then checked against real databases. The files of each fixture were applied, in the order the parser replays them (only the up sections of dbmate and goose), to PostgreSQL 17, MySQL 8.4 or SQLite 3 (`sqlite3 --safe`), in containers without network; their catalogs (`pg_catalog`, `information_schema`, the `PRAGMA` of SQLite) gave the same tables, columns (order, `NOT NULL`, primary keys), foreign keys (columns, referenced table and columns, `ON DELETE` / `ON UPDATE`), unique columns and indexes (columns, unique or not, partial, expressions). The types and the defaults were compared too, after normalization (`varchar(255)` is `character varying(255)`). The known differences:

- The databases of the Supabase projects lacked the schemas that Supabase creates: the roles, `auth.users`, `storage.buckets` and `storage.objects`, and the functions `auth.uid()`, `storage.foldername()` were created first. PostgreSQL 17 has no `vector` (pgvector) nor `http` extension: the columns of type `vector(n)` were created as `real[]`, without their `hnsw` / `ivfflat` indexes, in the copy applied to the database (the parser reads the files as they are). `pg-dump-pagila` uses `uuidv7()` of PostgreSQL 18, created as a function first.
- Harness creates its `migrations` table in code: its first migration alters it, so the parser adds it with the columns it sees (none) and a warning.
- `drizzle-openstatus` was applied up to `0040_narrow_anthem.sql`: the next migrations use `ALTER COLUMN ... TO` of libSQL (Turso), which SQLite does not have. The 95 migrations were compared with the output of the Drizzle parser on `test/fixtures/drizzle/openstatus` (the same commit): the same tables, columns and nullability, plus `status_reports_to_pages`, that the schema files no longer declare but no migration drops.
- `prisma-umami` was compared with the Prisma parser on `test/fixtures/prisma/umami` (the same commit) too: the same tables, columns and nullability (Umami uses `relationMode = "prisma"`: no foreign keys in the database).

The SQL is test data: the tests and the extension only read it. A 3 MB `db/structure.sql` of GitLab (not kept as a fixture) was checked the same way: 1094 tables, all identical, read in half a second.

## Hand-made

| Fixture | What it covers |
|---------|----------------|
| `pg-edge-cases/` | PostgreSQL, three Supabase migrations: names folded to lower case and quoted names, a schema of its own and the search path, identity, serial, arrays, enum types (`ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`, `RENAME VALUE`), generated columns, defaults with casts, a `CHECK`, a column named `fulltext` and one named `index`, nested comments, a transaction, functions with `$body$`, triggers, policies, grants, a view, a materialized view and its index, `DO` blocks (their branches, not their exception handler; the foreign keys of drizzle-kit 0.2x), `ALTER TABLE` (several actions, `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE ... USING`, `RENAME COLUMN`, `RENAME TO`, `SET SCHEMA`, constraints dropped by the name PostgreSQL gave them), the keys of `supabase db diff` (`PRIMARY KEY USING INDEX`, `NOT VALID` and `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`), partitions (`PARTITION OF`, `ATTACH PARTITION`), `INHERITS`, `LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL`, temporary and unlogged tables, `DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE`, `COPY ... FROM stdin` data, `COMMENT ON COLUMN` |
| `mysql-edge-cases/` | MySQL, Flyway (`V1`, `V1.1`, `V1_2`, `V2`, `V3` in a sub-folder, `V10`, a repeatable `R__` migration): backticks, `AUTO_INCREMENT`, table options, `enum` and `set`, unsigned and `zerofill`, `ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, `COMMENT`, `CHARACTER SET`, expression defaults, generated columns, executable comments, inline `KEY`, `UNIQUE KEY`, `FULLTEXT KEY` and prefix lengths, `DELIMITER` with a trigger and a procedure, `#` comments, `ADD COLUMN ... FIRST` / `AFTER`, `MODIFY`, `CHANGE`, `DROP FOREIGN KEY`, `DROP INDEX`, `RENAME INDEX`, `RENAME TABLE` (the foreign keys follow), `CREATE TABLE ... LIKE`, a dropped column removed from an index |
| `sqlite-edge-cases/` | SQLite, golang-migrate (`1`, `2`, `3`, `10`, with down files): `AUTOINCREMENT`, `[names]`, untyped columns, `ON CONFLICT`, `WITHOUT ROWID`, composite primary keys (nullable on SQLite), a trigger with semicolons in its body, a virtual table (FTS5), the table rebuild of prisma migrate (`PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF`, `new_posts` renamed), `RENAME COLUMN`, `DROP COLUMN`, `RENAME TO` (the foreign keys follow) |

To write `expected/` again after a change of the parser, run the parser on each fixture with the options above and check the differences one by one, then against the databases.
